source_contact.affiliation: School of Economics and Management, China University of Petroleum (East China)
source_contact.selection_basis: The open version of record marks Changsheng Huang as the corresponding author and publishes this institutional address. The article credits Yanpu Zhao with methodology/software and Mengjie Zhang with software/data curation, so the draft requests that the corresponding author involve the holders of the experiment source and data.

public_source_audit.outcome: The open article, DOI records, first-author ORCID, paper-linked GitHub repository, and exact DOI/title searches of public code/data registries expose only a two-file, single-F1 MATLAB example. They do not provide the full benchmark/CEC drivers, authoritative resolutions for the paper/code conflicts, seeds, raw trials, or statistics driver needed to close the preset and comparison gates.

sources.finding: The article supplies Equations 1-32, Algorithm 1, Tables 5-23, the corresponding-author address, and a link to the MATLAB repository. Its data-availability statement says the data are contained in the article, but no raw trials, seed schedule, batch/statistics driver, or supplemental archive is attached; the article and linked code leave the ten questions below unresolved.
The DOI record confirms the article and first-author ORCID, has an empty relation object, and links only the version-of-record PDF; it identifies no software, dataset, or supplement relation.
The DOAJ record links only the article full text and exposes no research-data, software, or supplementary object.

Yanpu Zhao's public ORCID record includes the AOBLMOA article and a SciProfiles identifier, but exposes no public email, software, dataset, or research-resource record supplying the missing experiment material.

The repository still resolves to the paper-audited commit and contains only AOBLMOA.m and main.m. The latter runs one unseeded F1 case; there are no other benchmark evaluators, CEC drivers, repeated-run/statistics scripts, saved configurations, or raw outputs.

A public repository-title search returned only the paper-linked SheldonYnuup/AOBLMOA repository. This records the indexed search outcome and does not prove that private or unindexed material is absent.
An exact-DOI public repository search returned zero repositories.
An exact-DOI public record search returned zero deposits; a separate AOBLMOA-title search also returned zero deposits.
An exact resource-DOI public article search returned zero deposits.
A public title search exposed no author-linked AOBLMOA experiment dataset.

blocking_questions.question: Which sex uses each Aquila strategy pair, and which exact fitness inequalities and equality cases select the Mayfly-versus-Aquila branch for males and females?
blocking_questions.known_evidence: The abstract assigns expanded strategies to males and narrowed strategies to females, while Equations 29-30 and the linked code do the opposite. Equation 30/code apply attraction when the female is worse than its paired male, but Algorithm 1 prints a conflicting female comparison. Equality behavior and the male equation's scalar-versus-coordinate global-best notation also require an executable resolution.
blocking_questions.required_answer_shape: For minimization and maximization, give the sex-to-X1/X2/X3/X4 mapping, exact branch predicates including equality and ties, global-best comparison semantics, and the authoritative source lines or corrected equations.
blocking_questions.units: sex, strategy IDs, objective comparisons, and branch decisions
acceptable_primary_evidence: A corrected, versioned AOBLMOA implementation and experiment driver
A publisher correction or dated author clarification identifying the authoritative equations and predicates

blocking_questions.question: In Equations 13, 16, and 30, is xM the per-coordinate mean across the relevant population, the scalar mean of the current candidate's coordinates used by the linked code, or another quantity?
blocking_questions.known_evidence: The article defines xM as the mean value of current-position solutions, while AOBLMOA.m calls mean(Mayflyf(i).Position) inside each female update. These produce different vectors and trajectories in more than one dimension.
blocking_questions.required_answer_shape: An executable formula identifying the population/candidate pool, axes reduced, lifecycle snapshot, sex, and whether the result is scalar or vector for every use of xM.
acceptable_primary_evidence: The exact MATLAB source used to generate Tables 5-23
A dated author clarification with a corrected formula and worked multidimensional example

blocking_questions.question: Did the reported AOBLMOA runs multiply the Mantegna Levy step by Equation 15's s=0.01, or use the unscaled Levy function in the linked MATLAB code?
blocking_questions.known_evidence: Equation 15 explicitly sets s=0.01. The linked Levy(d) function returns w/abs(v)^(1/beta) without that multiplier, so the published equation and linked code differ by a factor of 100.
blocking_questions.required_answer_shape: The exact Levy formula, beta and scale, draw granularity, and identification/checksum of the implementation used for every published experiment family.
acceptable_primary_evidence: The versioned Tables 5-23 implementation showing the applied scale
A dated author clarification resolving the Equation 15/code discrepancy

blocking_questions.question: What do the reported population size and lifecycle mean exactly: male/female/offspring counts, update order and snapshots, global/personal-best timing, crossover pairing, offspring sex assignment, and survivor replacement?
blocking_questions.known_evidence: The article reports population size 30, while main.m passes 30 males, 30 females, and 30 offspring. AOBLMOA.m updates every female before every male, uses evolving global-best state, splits flattened offspring by array order, and does not document whether this exact lifecycle generated every table. Mayfly currently uses frozen iteration-start snapshots and male-first processing.
blocking_questions.required_answer_shape: Exact per-sex and offspring counts plus ordered executable stages, live-versus-frozen reads, sort/tie rules, personal/global-best updates, parent pairs, offspring ordering/sex assignment, boundary repair, and truncation semantics.
blocking_questions.units: candidates, offspring, ordered stages, and state snapshots
acceptable_primary_evidence: The complete versioned experiment implementation and configuration
A dated author clarification defining every population and lifecycle convention
affected_fields: movement, mating, opposition, and survivor lifecycle

blocking_questions.question: Which objective calls are part of each reported run, and which calls are counted or omitted from any budget or complexity claim?
blocking_questions.known_evidence: The article limits the classic experiments by 1,000 iterations and gives no objective-call ceiling. The linked code increments funccount for moved males/females but not offspring, opposition candidates, repeated accepted-opposition evaluations, or history logging; different algorithms can therefore receive different numbers of calls under the same iteration count.
blocking_questions.required_answer_shape: A per-stage call ledger covering initialization, movement, offspring, opposition candidates, repeated evaluations, history/logging, constraints/penalties, stopping and final selection for each experiment family.
blocking_questions.units: objective and constraint evaluations per stage, iteration, and run
acceptable_primary_evidence: Instrumented original experiment drivers with a complete call trace
A dated author clarification defining the accounting and stopping convention

blocking_questions.question: Can the exact Tables 5-11 AOBLMOA and comparator implementations, all 19 benchmark evaluators, 30-run batch driver, and statistical-analysis driver be supplied?
blocking_questions.known_evidence: The linked repository contains only AOBLMOA.m and an unseeded, single-run F1 main.m. It omits F2-F19, comparator implementations/configurations, repeated-run orchestration, and the Wilcoxon/Friedman code.
blocking_questions.required_answer_shape: A versioned archive with checksums containing every evaluator, algorithm/configuration, run loop, output schema, timing convention/unit, standard-deviation convention, Wilcoxon implementation, Friedman tie handling, and software/toolbox versions.
blocking_questions.units: source files, checksums, algorithms, functions, runs, statistics, and time units
acceptable_primary_evidence: The original Tables 5-11 experiment archive
An author-controlled or publisher/institutional archival deposit

blocking_questions.question: What exact CEC2017 suite version, dimension, evaluation/stopping budget, transformations, comparator configurations, and handling of the removed F2 produced Table 13?
blocking_questions.known_evidence: The article reports 30 runs and 1,000 iterations but no dimension, objective-evaluation budget, seeds, or suite data version. It includes F2 although the final official CEC2017 suite removed that function, and the linked repository contains no CEC2017 evaluator or comparison driver.
blocking_questions.required_answer_shape: Versioned evaluator/data files and checksums; dimension and bounds; per-algorithm population and exact call/stopping budget; F2 provenance; comparator source/configuration; and the complete Table 13 driver.
blocking_questions.units: suite version, dimensions, candidates, iterations, and function evaluations
acceptable_primary_evidence: The original Table 13 CEC2017 experiment archive
A dated author clarification backed by the exact evaluator and driver

blocking_questions.question: What complete AOBLMOA protocol and feasibility/penalty semantics produced Tables 14-23 on the ten selected CEC2020 constrained problems?
blocking_questions.known_evidence: The article reports 25 runs and a static penalty but omits AOBLMOA population, iterations/evaluation budget, penalty definition/coefficient, violation aggregation, feasibility tolerance, table-value semantics, seeds, and feasibility outputs. The linked repository contains no CEC2020 evaluator or driver.
blocking_questions.required_answer_shape: Versioned official/modified evaluator and driver; exact problem-ID mapping; population/budget; penalty and feasibility rules; raw-objective-versus-penalized reporting; and all competition-required constraint-violation, feasibility-rate, and violation-count outputs.
blocking_questions.units: problem IDs, candidates, evaluations, objective values, constraint violations, tolerances, and feasible runs
acceptable_primary_evidence: The original Tables 14-23 constrained experiment archive
A dated author clarification plus the executable evaluator, penalty, and reporting driver

blocking_questions.question: Can the RNG identity and ordered seeds/states, raw per-run outputs, convergence histories, and intermediate statistics for every Tables 5-23 experiment and comparator be supplied?
blocking_questions.known_evidence: Neither the article nor repository provides seeds/states or ordered raw samples. Without them, the reported aggregates, standard deviations, rank-sum p-values, Friedman ranks, constrained feasibility, and historical pairing cannot be independently validated.
blocking_questions.required_answer_shape: Generator name/version and ordered seed or state mapping; one uniquely identified raw row per algorithm/function/problem/dimension/run; objective/cost, constraints, feasibility, calls, iterations and time; convergence histories; and scripts regenerating every table cell.
blocking_questions.units: generator states, runs, objective/fitness values, violations, evaluations, iterations, seconds, p-values, and ranks
acceptable_primary_evidence: The original author-supplied raw experiment archive
A publisher or institutional archive deposited by the authors

blocking_questions.question: What are the intended corrections and underlying raw values for the preserved table and official-suite inconsistencies?
blocking_questions.known_evidence: Table 8 F10 prints a standard deviation larger than its worst value; Table 13 contains missing AO/RSA F2 values with printed rank 8, an AOBLMOA F14 deviation of 3346 beside mean 1442, and an RSA F28 average below the official bias; Tables 14-23 conflict with official RC21/RC22 metadata, and Table 16's sCMAgES maximum differs from the official submission.
blocking_questions.required_answer_shape: A publisher correction or original unrounded samples/configuration identifying the intended value and provenance of every anomaly, including whether official suite/problem definitions or modified versions were used.
blocking_questions.units: objective statistics, ranks, problem dimensions/constraints, and source versions
acceptable_primary_evidence: The original table source and unrounded raw trials
A publisher correction or dated author clarification backed by the source data

requested_artifacts: The exact AOBLMOA and comparator implementations/configurations used for Tables 5-23
All classic, CEC2017, and CEC2020 evaluator/data files and complete batch/statistics drivers
The random-number generator and ordered seed/state schedules
Raw per-run objective, constraint, feasibility, evaluation, iteration, timing, convergence, and statistical outputs
A correction or authoritative resolution for every paper/code and paper/official-suite inconsistency

exact_preset_gate.rule: An aoblmoa-2023 exact algorithm preset may be added only after all five questions have non-null answers backed by cited primary evidence. The linked code's known g=0.9-to-0.4 schedule must also be implemented, and the resulting equations, population lifecycle, RNG order, opposition stage, boundary repair, and call ledger must pass source-conformance tests.

reproduction_comparison_gate.rule: A Tables 5-23 reproduction comparison additionally requires the relevant experiment-family questions and the shared raw-run/statistics questions to be resolved. Comparisons may be scoped to an independently closed family, but unavailable families and historical pairing must be identified explicitly and aggregate-only output must remain descriptive.

correspondence_draft.subject: Request for AOBLMOA Tables 5-23 implementation, protocol, and raw trial data
correspondence_draft.body:
Dear Professor Huang and co-authors,

I am implementing the protocol from your 2023 Biomimetics article, AOBLMOA: A Hybrid Biomimetic Optimization Algorithm for Numerical Optimization and Engineering Design Problems (doi:10.3390/biomimetics8040381), and would like to reproduce Tables 5-23 faithfully. The linked GitHub repository is valuable, but currently contains only AOBLMOA.m and a single-run F1 main.m. Could you please share the exact versioned AOBLMOA/comparator implementations, complete benchmark/CEC drivers and data, configurations, random-number generator and ordered seeds/states, and raw per-run outputs used for the article?

For an executable AOBLMOA preset, could you also clarify: (1) the authoritative sex-to-Aquila-strategy mapping and male/female branch inequalities, including equality; (2) whether xM is a population-coordinate mean or the current candidate's coordinate mean; (3) whether Levy steps use Equation 15's 0.01 scale or the linked code's unscaled form; (4) the meaning of population size 30 and the exact live/frozen update, best-tracking, crossover, offspring-sex, boundary, and survivor lifecycle; and (5) the complete objective/constraint-call accounting. For Tables 5-11, please include F1-F19, comparator and statistical drivers and timing/standard-deviation conventions. For Table 13, please identify the CEC2017 dimension, suite/F2 version, budget, and comparator configurations. For Tables 14-23, please provide the CEC2020 mapping, static-penalty and feasibility rules, budget, and constraint outputs. Original unrounded samples or corrections for the preserved Table 8, Table 13, RC21/RC22, and Table 16 inconsistencies would make the validation auditable.

Thank you for your time.
